\textbf{Collapse trajectory.}
Figure~\ref{fig:training-isr-curves} traces exec-only GRPO (seed~42) across 1000 training steps.
As PR climbs from $32\%$ to $96\%$, ISR$^*$ collapses from $0.642$ to $0.003$, a $214\times$ raw drop (partially attributable to premise-count inflation; matched comparison yields $1.06\times$, \S\ref{sec:goodhart}) consistent with structural degeneration behind apparent success. %% registry: plan003-eval-exec-only-r5, plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan016-extended-1000-s42
By 500 steps, $87\%$ of proved samples embed the conclusion verbatim (CE), establishing degeneration independent of the ISR scalar.
A binary variant testing only collective premise necessity misses the collapse entirely ($\text{ISR}{=}1.0$ for all proved samples), confirming that per-component LOO testing is essential (Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}).
All three exec-only seeds converge to ${\leq}6.2\%$ non-hacking by 1000 steps (Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}), confirming that structural degeneration under exec-only reward is not seed-specific among converged runs.

\textbf{Cross-seed instability.}
Three seeds diverge into qualitatively different failure modes: conclusion embedding (s42), repetition collapse (s43), and tautological collapse (s44), yet all converge to ${\leq}7\%$ non-hacking by 1000 steps (Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}; Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}).
Exec-only seeds exhibit qualitatively different convergence patterns (PR range: 13--98\%), precluding meaningful pooling; we report seed~42 as representative of the converged regime (Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}). %% registry: plan001-exec-only-s42-r2, plan001-exec-only-s43-r4, plan001-exec-only-s44; plan016-extended-1000-s42, plan001-exec-only-s43-1000-r7, plan001-exec-only-s44-1000-r2
Two additional seeds under identical conditions fail to converge ($\text{PR}{\approx}14\%$; Appendix~\ref{app:seed-convergence}), retaining genuine reasoning and suggesting that structural degeneration requires successful convergence, though the confound between model capability and optimization success precludes strong causal attribution (Appendix~\ref{app:llama-coldstart}).

\textbf{SFT baseline.}
SFT on gold formalizations produces $92\%$ non-hacking outputs at $\text{PR}{=}13\%$ (odds ratio ${=}147$ vs.\ exec-only, $p{<}0.001$), establishing that hacking modes are absent before RL optimization.
SFT serves as a pre-RL reference rather than a PR-matched control; its low PR reflects minimal optimization pressure.
Early-training comparison supports this interpretation: at 100 steps ($\text{PR}{=}32\%$), hacking already reaches $31\%$ vs.\ SFT's $8\%$ at comparable PR (Appendix~\ref{app:100step}). %% registry: plan009-sft-baseline-s42-1000/s43-1000/s44-1000-r3

\subsection{Goodhart Effects on ISR-as-Reward}
\label{sec:goodhart}

We reverse ISR's role from observer to reward: $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, with matched random control ($u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$).
The result is a regressional Goodhart pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: optimizing a structural proxy shifts the \emph{composition} of failure modes without reducing their aggregate prevalence.
ISR reward systematically selects for tautological shortcuts (TS) over conclusion embedding (CE) rather than producing genuine reasoning (Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}). The scalar ISR$^*$ advantage ($214\times$ raw) collapses to $1.06\times$ after controlling for premise count; the compositional mode shift provides the primary evidence.

\paragraph{Multiplicative coupling.}
Three controls constrain the multiplicative confound: exec-only's convergence to pure hacking, the qualitative TS shift under ISR, and an additive variant that did not converge (Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).
The shuffled-ISR control ($87\%$ non-hacking at low PR) confirms the Goodhart effect requires sample-level ISR signal, not its distributional shape.

\textbf{Low-dose ISR ($\beta{=}0.1$).}
ISR reward amplifies TS convergence: $71\%$ of proved samples under ISR exhibit tautological shortcuts vs.\ $14\%$ under random (Appendix~\ref{app:statistical-details}). %% registry: plan002 vs plan018 all seeds; D095 FINAL
TS is the canonical Goodhart move: a single premise identical to the conclusion yields $\text{ISR}\geq 0.5$ by construction, directly satisfying the LOO metric (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}).
Total conclusion embedding ($\text{CE}+\text{TS}$) spans $68$--$100\%$ across both conditions; the composition shifts (CE dominates under random, TS under ISR) without reducing aggregate hacking (Figure~\ref{fig:hacking-composition}).
A seed-stratified $\chi^2$ test confirms the overall mode distribution differs significantly between ISR and random conditions ($\chi^2{=}174.8$, $\text{df}{=}2$, $p{<}10^{-38}$; Appendix~\ref{app:statistical-details}).

\textbf{Seed-dependent outcomes.}
ISR reward produces bimodal outcomes (Figure~\ref{fig:seed-divergence}): 3 of 5 seeds converge to gaming, demonstrating that the Goodhart effect can occur under standard training conditions (95\% Clopper--Pearson CI: [11.8\%, 88.1\%]; $n{=}5$); 2 of 5 retain substantial genuine reasoning (seeds~45/46 added post-hoc to test replication; Appendix~\ref{app:detailed-results}).
Excluding seed~43 (which uses nucleus sampling; \S\ref{sec:setup}), the remaining two ISR seeds show ${\leq}7\%$ non-hacking and $100\%$ TS, strengthening the core finding (full $N{=}2$ analysis: Appendix~\ref{app:n2-sensitivity}).

\textbf{Premise-count confound.}
The $214\times$ raw ISR$^*$ collapse is largely explained by premise-count reduction: ISR-trained models produce shorter formalizations that mechanically inflate ISR.

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Execution-based evaluation of neurosymbolic reasoning conflates faithful derivation with structural shortcuts: a formalization that trivially embeds the conclusion among its premises proves just as reliably as a genuine one, and reinforcement learning (RL) optimizers exploit this indifference.
3	We apply leave-one-out ablation to GRPO-trained formalizations---\emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA)---testing whether each component is individually necessary for proof success, and characterize structural degeneration under six reward conditions via the resulting \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR).
4	ISR reveals that prove-rate gains conceal a compositional shift toward hacking modes, but ISR occupies a paradoxical position: the same leave-one-out structure that makes it informative also makes it gameable.
5	Tautological formalizations satisfy the necessity criterion by construction, so when ISR is repurposed as a training reward, the model learns to game the diagnostic rather than the task.
6	In our Qwen3-4B experiments, the resulting Goodhart effect is seed-dependent (3 of 5 seeds converge to gaming, demonstrating that the Goodhart effect can occur under standard training conditions; 2 of 5 retain genuine reasoning), but the \emph{observe-vs-optimize asymmetry} persists across logic types and dataset families---confirmed by cross-logic (Prolog) replication and supported by exploratory cross-benchmark (ProofFOL) evidence: structural proxies for formalization integrity are easier to observe than to optimize.\end{abstract}
7

28	In our Qwen3-4B experiments, the asymmetry persists across logic types (FOL, Prolog), dataset families (FOLIO, ProofFOL), reward doses, and random seeds, suggesting that structural proxies for formalization integrity are easier to observe than to optimize.
29	
30	We contribute:
31	(\textbf{C1})~a systematic empirical analysis of structural degeneration in GRPO-trained neurosymbolic reasoning, using LOO ablation (STA/ISR) to catalogue eight hacking modes across six reward conditions (\S\S\ref{sec:sta}--\ref{sec:crossdomain});
32	(\textbf{C2})~empirical characterization of a seed-dependent Goodhart effect when ISR is repurposed as reward, with matched controls ruling out confounds (\S\ref{sec:goodhart});
33	(\textbf{C3})~cross-logic replication (FOL/Prolog) confirming that the Goodhart effect transfers across logic types, with exploratory cross-dataset evidence (FOLIO/ProofFOL; \S\ref{sec:crossdomain}).

An ISR of zero for proved samples can arise from structural degeneration or genuine redundancy; our hacking mode classification (\S\ref{sec:taxonomy-method}) disambiguates these cases, with ${>}90\%$ of low-ISR proved samples exhibiting identifiable hacking patterns.

\section{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

Experiments use a single base model (Qwen3-4B); structural degeneration patterns may not transfer to other model families, and cross-scale generalization remains untested (Appendix~\ref{app:8b-results}).
Three to five seeds per condition demonstrate qualitative divergence but remain underpowered for seed-level significance; pooled statistics treat within-seed samples as independent.
The mechanisms driving seed heterogeneity---why 3/5 seeds converge to gaming while 2/5 retain genuine reasoning under identical conditions---remain unexplored; possible explanations include initialization sensitivity, early-training bifurcation dynamics, and loss landscape multi-modality, but causal attribution requires targeted intervention experiments beyond our current scope.
FOLIO is a relatively small (1,435 examples) synthetic benchmark; generalization of both the degeneration phenomena and the STA diagnostic to larger, naturalistic, or domain-specific corpora (e.g., legal or scientific reasoning) is untested.
ISR quantifies component necessity, not semantic faithfulness; its diagnostic value is realized through the mode breakdown, not the scalar alone (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
Given perfect classifier precision (152/152; Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}), measured non-hacking rates of 6--10\% for converged seeds are internally consistent only if classifier recall exceeds ${\sim}90\%$; below this threshold, the implied true non-hacking rate would be negative, indicating that low measured rates are self-validating evidence of high recall.

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Execution-based evaluation of neurosymbolic reasoning conflates faithful derivation with structural shortcuts: a formalization that trivially embeds the conclusion among its premises proves just as reliably as a genuine one, and reinforcement learning (RL) optimizers exploit this indifference.
3	We apply leave-one-out ablation to GRPO-trained formalizations---\emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA)---testing whether each component is individually necessary for proof success, and characterize structural degeneration under six reward conditions via the resulting \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR).
4	ISR reveals that prove-rate gains conceal a compositional shift toward hacking modes, but ISR occupies a paradoxical position: the same leave-one-out structure that makes it informative also makes it gameable.
5	Tautological formalizations satisfy the necessity criterion by construction, so when ISR is repurposed as a training reward, the model learns to game the diagnostic rather than the task.
6	In our Qwen3-4B experiments, the resulting Goodhart effect is seed-dependent (3 of 5 seeds converge to gaming, demonstrating that the Goodhart effect can occur under standard training conditions; 2 of 5 retain genuine reasoning), but the \emph{observe-vs-optimize asymmetry} persists across logic types and dataset families---confirmed by cross-logic (Prolog) replication and supported by exploratory cross-benchmark (ProofFOL) evidence: structural proxies for formalization integrity are easier to observe than to optimize.\end{abstract}
7

47	\subsection{Goodhart Effects on ISR-as-Reward}
48	\label{sec:goodhart}
49	
50	We reverse ISR's role from observer to reward: $r = r_{\text{exec}}\cdot(1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, with matched random control ($u\sim\mathcal{U}(0,1)$).
51	The result is a regressional Goodhart pattern~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: optimizing a structural proxy shifts the \emph{composition} of failure modes without reducing their aggregate prevalence.
52	ISR reward systematically selects for tautological shortcuts (TS) over conclusion embedding (CE) rather than producing genuine reasoning (Table~\ref{tab:goodhart-landscape}). The scalar ISR$^*$ advantage ($214\times$ raw) collapses to $1.06\times$ after controlling for premise count; the compositional mode shift provides the primary evidence.
53	
54	\paragraph{Multiplicative coupling.}
55	Three controls constrain the multiplicative confound: exec-only's convergence to pure hacking, the qualitative TS shift under ISR, and an additive variant that did not converge (Appendix~\ref{app:setup}).

\subsection{Seed-Dependent Convergence in Exec-Only GRPO}
\label{app:seed-convergence}

Not all exec-only seeds converge.
Of 6 seeds tested (s42--s46, s52; s52 uses $K{=}4$, all others $K{=}8$), we observe three regimes: \emph{converging with degeneration} (s42: $\text{PR}{=}93\%$, genuine${=}7.5\%$; s44: $\text{PR}{=}96\%$, genuine${=}0\%$; s46: $\text{PR}{=}93\%$ at 500 steps), \emph{slow convergence with degeneration} (s43: $\text{PR}{=}14\%$ but $100\%$ hacking at 500 steps), and \emph{non-converging} (s45: $\text{PR}{=}15\%$, genuine${=}86.7\%$; s52: $\text{PR}{=}14\%$, genuine${=}85.7\%$).
Non-converging seeds retain high genuine rates (85--87\%), indicating that structural degeneration is conditional on successful RL optimization: when GRPO fails to bootstrap prove rate beyond base-model levels, the model preserves structural integrity.
Extended training to 1000 steps for s45 confirms persistent non-convergence ($\text{PR}{=}15\%$, $\text{ISR}^*{=}0.592$, genuine${=}86.7\%$, $n{=}15$ proved); the model neither improves nor degenerates.

This parallels the LLaMA-3.2-3B finding (Appendix~\ref{app:llama-coldstart}), where GRPO also fails to improve PR and retains structural quality.
Both cases support the interpretation that degeneration is a byproduct of reward optimization success, not of the training procedure per se.

1	\begin{abstract}
2	Execution-based evaluation of neurosymbolic reasoning conflates faithful derivation with structural shortcuts: a formalization that trivially embeds the conclusion among its premises proves just as reliably as a genuine one, and reinforcement learning (RL) optimizers exploit this indifference.
3	We apply leave-one-out ablation to GRPO-trained formalizations---\emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA)---testing whether each component is individually necessary for proof success, and characterize structural degeneration under six reward conditions via the resulting \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR).

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation; repurposed as reward, ISR produces a seed-dependent Goodhart effect: structural proxies for formalization integrity are easier to observe than to optimize (Appendix~\ref{app:practical-guidelines}).
Cross-logic experiments (Prolog) confirm the compositional mode shift; cross-benchmark evidence (ProofFOL, $p{=}0.10$) is exploratory (\S\ref{sec:crossdomain}).
Convergence appears necessary for degeneration (Appendix~\ref{app:seed-convergence}); for practitioners, structural diagnostics should be applied post-hoc, with the mode breakdown providing the reliable signal.
The observe-vs-optimize asymmetry motivates targeted mitigations---mode-aware reward shaping~\citep{tarek2025reward, pronesti2026beyond} or single-premise penalties---over blanket structural optimization; that 2/5 seeds retain genuine reasoning suggests this is feasible.
Remaining open questions include disentangling LOO's premise-count bias from genuine complexity and extending our hacking taxonomy to process reward settings.

1	\section{Limitations}
2	\label{sec:limitations}
3	
4	Experiments use a single base model (Qwen3-4B); structural degeneration patterns may not transfer to other model families, and cross-scale generalization remains untested (Appendix~\ref{app:8b-results}).
5	Three to five seeds per condition demonstrate qualitative divergence but remain underpowered for seed-level significance; pooled statistics treat within-seed samples as independent.
6	Seeds 45 and 46 were added post-hoc after observing bimodal behavior in seeds 42--44; the 3/5 gaming rate should therefore be interpreted as an existence demonstration rather than a prevalence estimate.
7	The mechanisms driving seed heterogeneity---why 3/5 seeds converge to gaming while 2/5 retain genuine reasoning under identical conditions---remain unexplored; possible explanations include initialization sensitivity, early-training bifurcation dynamics, and loss landscape multi-modality, but causal attribution requires targeted intervention experiments beyond our current scope.
8	FOLIO is a relatively small (1,435 examples) synthetic benchmark; generalization of both the degeneration phenomena and the STA diagnostic to larger, naturalistic, or domain-specific corpora (e.g., legal or scientific reasoning) is untested.
9	ISR quantifies component necessity, not semantic faithfulness; its diagnostic value is realized through the mode breakdown, not the scalar alone (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
10	Given perfect classifier precision (152/152; Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}), measured non-hacking rates of 6--10\% for converged seeds are internally consistent only if classifier recall exceeds ${\sim}90\%$; below this threshold, the implied true non-hacking rate would be negative, indicating that low measured rates are self-validating evidence of high recall.

\section{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

Experiments use a single base model (Qwen3-4B); structural degeneration patterns may not transfer to other model families, and cross-scale generalization remains untested (Appendix~\ref{app:8b-results}).
Three to five seeds per condition demonstrate qualitative divergence but remain underpowered for seed-level significance; pooled statistics treat within-seed samples as independent.
Seeds 45 and 46 were added post-hoc after observing bimodal behavior in seeds 42--44; the 3/5 gaming rate should therefore be interpreted as an existence demonstration rather than a prevalence estimate.
The mechanisms driving seed heterogeneity---why 3/5 seeds converge to gaming while 2/5 retain genuine reasoning under identical conditions---remain unexplored; possible explanations include initialization sensitivity, early-training bifurcation dynamics, and loss landscape multi-modality, but causal attribution requires targeted intervention experiments beyond our current scope.
FOLIO is a relatively small (1,435 examples) synthetic benchmark; generalization of both the degeneration phenomena and the STA diagnostic to larger, naturalistic, or domain-specific corpora (e.g., legal or scientific reasoning) is untested.
ISR quantifies component necessity, not semantic faithfulness; its diagnostic value is realized through the mode breakdown, not the scalar alone (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).
Given perfect classifier precision (152/152; Appendix~\ref{app:hacking-modes}), measured non-hacking rates of 6--10\% for converged seeds are internally consistent only if classifier recall exceeds ${\sim}90\%$; below this threshold, the implied true non-hacking rate would be negative, indicating that low measured rates are self-validating evidence of high recall.
Code, training scripts, and evaluation data will be released upon acceptance.
